scope: security, Firestore rules, booking integrity, referral abuse, auth flows, data model and cost

finders.prompt: Attack firestore.rules as three actors: an unauthenticated visitor, a verified signed-in client, and an invited (role admin) team member. For every match block and helper function, ask: what can this actor create, read, update, delete, and is any of it more than the docs/SETUP-firebase.md data-model table promises? Look specifically at: quoteFields (which fields a stranger may set, including refAmount, discount, estimate* and whether an admin page or email trusts them); invited() granting admin powers from adminInvites alone; holds being world-readable (what is exposed: dates, slots, requestIds, segments, forever); whether hold creation validates the date against days/{date} closed days, leadDays, horizon, weekdays, or capacity at all; delete rules that use get() on another user's document; list vs get on referrers; credits; shifts; whether request.resource.data.diff is used safely; and whether any rule function can be bypassed by omitting a field or using an unexpected type. Cross-check each path against the JavaScript that uses it (backend.js, admin.js, account.js, referral.js) so you report real gaps, not theoretical ones.

Audit the client-side web security of every page and script: every innerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML sink in app.js, quote.js, admin.js, timeclock.js, account.js, referral.js, calendar.js, availability.js, i18n.js and whether every interpolated value passes through the escaper (esc/A.esc), including values from Firestore that an attacker-controlled request can contain (name, notes, company, email, ref) and values from the URL (?ref=, ?lang=, ?signup=, ?date=, email-link parameters); open-redirect or URL-building issues; the public Formspree endpoint in plans.js (anyone can POST to it: spam, exhausting the 50/month quota, forged 'requests' in the owner's inbox that bypass Firestore); the App Check key and monitor-only mode; CSV export injection in timeclock.js (formulas starting with = + - @); the admin page being a public URL; sign-in flows (email link storage, password reset, Google popup); missing security headers in firebase.json (CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, frame-ancestors); third-party script/vendor integrity (Firebase SDK pinned at 10.14.1 via Hosting reserved URLs, Google Fonts, vendor/qrcode.js). Report concrete, exploitable or policy-relevant items with the sink and the source named.

Audit the booking and calendar logic end to end: plans.js availability settings, calendar.js, availability.js, quote.js (date/slot step), backend.js (how requests and holds are written, read, moved, cancelled; listeners), admin.js (confirm/decline/done, close day, block window, phone bookings with requestId manual), account.js (client move/cancel) and firestore.rules. Look for: capacity being enforced only in page code (two visitors can hold the same last window; what the rules allow); holds for past dates, closed days, blocked windows, days outside weekdays or horizon; date/time handling across time zones and DST (dates as YYYY-MM-DD strings, 'today' computed in the visitor's browser versus Charlotte time; the 24-hour change-notice computation in account.js; the after-hours commercial slot); what happens to a hold when a request is declined, done, deleted, or moved by an admin; stale holds; the manual booking path; the week-ahead panel; recurring plans being booked as a single date with no series or next-visit concept; and anything a visitor could do to fill the calendar. Run calendar.js in node or Chromium with fake dates where that settles a claim.

Audit the refer-a-friend and credits system for abuse and errors: referral.js (code capture from ?ref=, persistence, banner, QR), account.js (code creation: the users + referrers two-document write and whether it is atomic and retried; ledger display), quote.js and backend.js (how ref, refAmount, refDropped reach the request; what the rules verify), admin.js (granting friend and referrer credits on confirm/done, duplicate-credit prevention, repeat-customer detection by email or phone and how phone numbers are normalised, applying credit up to maxPercentOfVisit, undo, adjustments, deletion), firestore.rules (credits write admin-only, refOk, refAmount settable by the client), plans.js referral settings, refer.html and the i18n copy promising amounts. Look for: self-referral with a second email; a referrer getting paid for a friend who never pays; credits granted twice via confirm then done or via a move back to new; the client-supplied refAmount being displayed or applied as if trusted; code enumeration; the banner or stored code lingering after the program is disabled; copy that promises something the code does not do.

Audit sign-in and identity in backend.js, account.js, admin.js, quote.js and firestore.rules: Google popup versus redirect on mobile Safari and in-app browsers with authDomain overridden to the site's own domain; email-link sign-in (where the email is stored, the same-device requirement, the link landing on account.html, expiry, error states); email+password accounts that are unverified (rules require email_verified for reading requests: what the client actually sees, is the verification prompt clear, resend); password reset; the admin page using invited() so an invited person has admin rights before any admins document exists; who can see whom in Team; sign-out and localStorage mkg.account flag drift; session persistence choice; what happens when a client's email on a request differs in case or has a plus-alias; account linking when the same email uses Google and password; the signed-in quote form locking the email. Report concrete failure modes with the lines involved.

Audit the Firestore data model and its operating cost and privacy: how admin.js and account.js query and listen (whole-collection listeners on requests, holds, shifts, credits; unbounded growth; missing composite indexes that would make a query fail in production; pagination); holds and days being world-readable forever (what a scraper learns, no cleanup of old holds); PII retention with no deletion path for clients (privacy.html promises versus reality); backups and export; the rules being pasted by hand while firebase.json declares them (drift risk; the deploy workflow only deploys hosting); App Check in monitor-only mode so bots can write; the free-tier limits and the $1 budget alert; Formspree quota; whether the request document stores everything the admin needs or relies on client-computed estimates; and whether any field is written in two places inconsistently (status values, updatedAt, source phone). Report items that will bite the owner as the business grows, each anchored in code.

scope: JavaScript behaviour and bugs in every page script

finders.prompt: Audit app.js and plans.js as the pricing and plans engine: the per-visit formula (base + per[dim] x size) x (1 - discount), rounding and currency formatting (dollars()), the monthly figure for commercial (visitsPerMonth), the follow-up tiers (uses versus discount), the dial on the home page, the plan cards and comparison table rendering, the segment switch (window.MKG_SEGMENT), state saved to localStorage (STORAGE_KEY schema: what happens when saved state has an id that no longer exists, a dim out of range, or comes from the other segment), defaults, min/max/step clamping on the steppers, keyboard and rapid-click behaviour, NaN or undefined paths, and whether the numbers shown on index.html, plans.html, quote.html and in the request payload are computed by the same code and agree. Execute app.js in node with a jsdom-free harness or in Chromium to check actual outputs for several sizes and frequencies.

Audit quote.js (and quote.html / commercial-quote.html) step by step: ZIP validation and serviceZips/outOfArea; the space step; plan and schedule; contact (name, email, phone validation; contactMethod; days; timeOfDay); the when step (calendar, date and slot carried from availability.html via URL or storage, what if none picked); review; the draft saved in sessionStorage (restore on reload, stale drafts, clearing after submit); the exact payload() versus the quoteFields allow-list in firestore.rules (a field name, type, or length mismatch means Firestore silently rejects the request and the visitor sees a failure or, worse, a success); the submit path with Promise.race on the Formspree notify (8 seconds) and the Firestore write (ordering, double-submit protection, what the visitor sees on each failure combination, the demo path when backend is absent); signed-in prefill and the locked email; the follow-up tier UI; the _subject field; the book-again path from account.html; browser back/forward and refresh mid-flow. Walk the flow in Chromium at http://127.0.0.1:8787/quote.html and commercial-quote.html, in EN and ES.

Audit backend.js as the Firestore and Auth wrapper: SDK loading order and failure handling (script(), init.json, App Check activation, the useEmu path); submitRequest (id generation, the batched request + hold write, createdAt as serverTimestamp versus the rule createdAt == request.time, holdPath keyed by request id, segment on the hold, what is sent when no date is chosen); move and cancel (field sets versus the rules' customerMoves and customerCancels: movedFrom, movedByClientAt, updatedAt, status transitions, hold replacement); the calendar reads (holds query shape, days doc, capacity counting, segment filtering); listeners and their cleanup on page navigation; error mapping to i18n keys; the auth helpers (onAuth, sign-in methods, the LINK_KEY email storage, isAdmin resolution via admins doc versus adminInvites); and every exported function's behaviour when db is null. Compare each write against firestore.rules line by line and report any mismatch that would be rejected in production.

Audit admin.js and timeclock.js (the owner and staff page): request cards and status transitions (new, confirmed, declined, done, cancelled), the DELETE/BORRAR confirmation, note to client, payment link, final price, service/plan change, date and window moves and their hold updates, credits granting hooks on confirm/done, search, the week-ahead panel, the calendar column (close day, block window, phone bookings and the manual hold, removing one), the Team panel (invite, remove, owner protection), the Credits tab (balances, ledger, apply, undo, adjust, delete), the time clock (clock in/out, open-shift detection, shift edits versus the rules' changed().hasOnly, hours and dollars-per-hour math, week/month/last-7/30 ranges and their time zone, the CSV export: escaping, timezone of timestamps, formula injection), tab-title counter, listeners, and failure states (permission denied, offline). Check each Firestore write against firestore.rules. The page cannot connect locally, so reason from code and exercise pure functions in node where possible.

Audit account.js, availability.js and referral.js: the request list rendering and status labels in both languages; the move and cancel buttons and the 24-hour notice computation (policy.changeNoticeHours, time zone, slot start time parsing from the slot label or id, confirmed-only logic); the Pay online button and which link wins; the sign-in forms (password, create account, email link, reset, verification resend) and their error messages; the ?signup=1 and prefill email path from quote.js; handling of Firebase action links landing on account.html; the referral code creation (users + referrers; retries on collision; what the client sees while creating); the invite link and QR generation (vendor/qrcode.js usage, download of the QR card, canvas sizing); the ?ref= capture, expiry, banner, dismissal in sessionStorage, and whether a code is still sent when referral.enabled is false; availability.html's segment switch and the handoff of a picked day and window into the quote pages. Run the pages in Chromium (not-connected mode) and exercise what you can; reason from code for the rest.

Audit i18n.js (the engine part, roughly the last 150 lines, plus how keys are structured) and calendar.js: language detection and persistence (?lang=, localStorage, navigator.language, html lang attribute update, document.title and meta description updates, the data-i18n and data-i18n-attr mechanisms, the {placeholder} substitution with LIVE values and its escaping, commercial:<key> fallback), what happens with a missing key (is the key shown raw?), re-applying translations to content rendered later by other scripts (plan cards, calendar, request cards: do they re-render on language switch or go stale?), pluralisation and number/date formatting per language (toLocaleDateString with which locale, currency formatting, 12-hour times in Spanish); calendar.js month navigation, min and max bounds (leadDays, horizonDays), today detection and time zone, weekday headers in Spanish, aria roles and keyboard navigation of the grid, disabled days, capacity display, the hold counting by segment, and re-rendering on language switch. Run things in Chromium to confirm; findings must be reproducible.

scope: accessibility, performance, SEO, responsive layout, and bilingual copy quality

finders.prompt: Audit accessibility of the static markup and styles across all 13 HTML pages and styles.css: landmark and heading structure, form labels and error association (aria-describedby, aria-invalid, aria-live for step changes and submit results), the EN/ES toggle and the html lang attribute, image alt text (including the logo pictures and decorative SVGs), link text, colour contrast of the tokens in styles.css (lemon #ffd93b on paper, pine on mist, muted text, text on the pine/on-dark sections, focus ring on dark), focus-visible handling, target sizes under 24x24 CSS px, skip link, reduced-motion, the comparison table semantics (scope, headers), the plan cards' expandable includes, and anything hidden with display:none that should be reachable. Run axe-core via Playwright on every page in both languages and at 390px and 1280px widths, read the violations, and triage them (not every axe rule is worth reporting; report the ones with real user impact, with the selector and the file/line that produces the markup).

Audit keyboard and screen-reader operation of the interactive widgets, by driving them with Playwright keyboard events and inspecting the DOM: the home-page plan dial and steppers (app.js), the segmented frequency control and plan selection (role, aria-pressed/aria-checked, arrow keys), the quote form steps (focus moved to the new step's heading? errors announced? the stepper buttons, the days chips, the calendar grid in calendar.js: roles, aria-selected, arrow-key movement, disabled days, month buttons, and how a chosen day and slot are announced), the FAQ accordions, the language toggle, the referral banner dismiss, the admin cards' buttons and dialogs, account.html sign-in forms, and the quote confirmation. Also check that dynamically rendered HTML (innerHTML) gets translated and keeps its ARIA on language switch. Report defects with the file and line that render the control.

Audit page weight and loading: measure with Playwright (request sizes and timings, DOMContentLoaded, LCP element, CLS if you can compute it) at http://127.0.0.1:8787/ for index.html, plans.html, quote.html, commercial.html and availability.html. Look at: brand/ image choices and sizes (which PNGs and WebPs are actually requested per page, the 1.2MB logo-full-1024.png as og:image, favicon-512.png at 390KB, apple-touch-icon 67KB), missing width/height or fetchpriority/preload for the LCP image, the Google Fonts request (5 weights of a variable font, display=swap, render-blocking CSS), scripts loaded synchronously at the end of body (plans.js, i18n.js at 1776 lines unminified, app.js, backend.js and then three Firebase compat SDK scripts plus App Check loaded sequentially with async=false), the ?v=22 cache-busting versus firebase.json Cache-Control max-age=0 must-revalidate on every html/js/css (no long-lived caching even though files are versioned; images get Hosting's default), no minification or compression settings, duplicated inline SVGs, CSS size, and layout shift from late-translated text. Quantify each item and say what the user would notice on a phone on 4G.

Audit search visibility: read the head of every HTML page and sitemap.xml, robots.txt, firebase.json. Check: hreflang links use relative URLs and point at ?lang= variants (validity, consistency with canonical, x-default), the Spanish version being client-side only (crawlers see English; html lang stays en until JS runs; no indexable Spanish URLs), title and meta description per page and language (set via data-i18n at runtime), canonical tags, duplicate content between index.html and / and ?lang= variants, the LocalBusiness JSON-LD (missing priceRange, openingHours, geo, sameAs, hasOfferCatalog or Service markup, areaServed as a City object), Organization versus LocalBusiness subtype (HomeAndConstructionBusiness or similar), FAQPage markup opportunity for the FAQ, BreadcrumbList, og:image aspect and size for Facebook and iMessage, twitter:card, whether admin.html, account.html, availability.html should be noindex (and are listed in the sitemap or not), 404 page (none in repo), cleanUrls in firebase.json (.html in URLs), www versus apex, sitemap lastmod accuracy, internal linking and anchor text, headings per page, image alt text for SEO, page speed signals, and local SEO basics (NAP consistency, service-area pages, Google Business Profile link). Report what measurably affects ranking or sharing, anchored to file and line.

Audit the visual layout by rendering every page (index, plans, quote with each step, commercial, commercial-plans, commercial-quote, availability, account, admin, refer, privacy, terms) with Playwright in EN and ES at widths 320, 360, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 px, saving full-page screenshots to your scratch dir and LOOKING at them with the Read tool. Also detect programmatically: horizontal overflow (document.scrollWidth > innerWidth), elements wider than the viewport, text clipped by overflow hidden, tap targets smaller than 44x44 on mobile, sticky header overlapping content or anchors, the comparison table and the calendar grid on narrow screens, long Spanish strings breaking buttons or the segmented controls, the plan dial at 320px, font sizes under 16px in inputs (iOS zoom), and anything that changes between EN and ES. Report each defect with the breakpoint, the screenshot path, and the styles.css or HTML line that causes it.

Audit the bilingual copy and its wiring: parse i18n.js and check EN/ES key parity (keys missing in one language, empty strings, English text left in the ES map, placeholders present in one language but not the other, commercial: overrides without a base); collect every data-i18n and data-i18n-attr key used in all 13 HTML files and every t('...') call in the JS files and verify each exists in both languages; find hardcoded user-visible strings that bypass i18n (aria-labels, alt text, title attributes, button text, confirm() dialogs, console-facing errors shown to users, the Formspree email subject and body, CSV headers, the schema.org text, the quote review labels, status words), Spanish quality (accents and ñ, tú versus usted consistency across pages, gender agreement, anglicisms, regional fit for Charlotte's Spanish-speaking community, formal legal text on privacy and terms), currency and date formats per language (toLocale* calls and their locale arguments), and whether the <title>, meta description, og tags, and html lang switch. Produce a precise list; a script in your scratch dir is the right tool.

scope: user experience, conversion, pricing logic and presentation, content, legal, and growth gaps versus the plan

finders.prompt: Walk the residential customer journey as a Charlotte homeowner on a phone: http://127.0.0.1:8787/index.html, then plans.html, then quote.html through all six steps to the review and the demo confirmation, then availability.html and the handoff back into the quote, in English and then in Spanish, using Playwright at 390px (take screenshots and read them). Evaluate clarity of the value proposition and plan names, the live dial, the 'Commercial service' card placement, the nav, CTAs and their wording, trust signals (who are we, insurance, photos, reviews: the site deliberately has none, so what does it offer instead?), the FAQ coverage, the price-is-an-estimate messaging, friction in each quote step (field count, validation messages, the ZIP step with no serviceZips configured, the days and time-of-day chips, the calendar step when nothing is chosen), the confirmation and what the customer is told happens next, and the account creation offer. Report concrete, prioritised UX defects and missing elements anchored to the HTML, i18n.js or JS lines that produce them.

Walk the commercial customer journey as an office manager comparing cleaning vendors: http://127.0.0.1:8787/commercial.html, commercial-plans.html, commercial-quote.html (all steps), in English and Spanish at both 390px and 1280px with Playwright, reading screenshots. Evaluate B2B expectations (certificate of insurance, bonding, background checks, after-hours access and key handling, supplies, walkthrough before quoting, a written proposal, W-9 or invoicing terms, contract length and the 'no contracts' promise applied to businesses), the square-foot and restroom estimator (step 250, max 20000, the approximate monthly figure, visits-per-week ladder, the Mon-Fri 35% discount sanity), facility type options, the 'Residential service' mirror card, copy that is clearly residential copy reused (commercial:<key> fallbacks that read oddly), the quote fields (company, floors, requestedTime, after-hours slot), and the confirmation. Report prioritised defects and gaps anchored to files and lines.

Evaluate the client account page and the owner's admin page as products: read account.html, account.js, admin.html, admin.js, timeclock.js, calendar.js, docs/SETUP-firebase.md, and render both pages at http://127.0.0.1:8787/ (not-connected mode) at 390px and 1280px to judge layout and information architecture. For the client: what they can and cannot do (move, cancel, pay, see notes, see credits, rebook), what they are not told (no confirmation email, no reminder, no receipt), the sign-in options and whether a non-technical client will manage, the 24-hour cutoff messaging. For the owner: the daily workflow (new requests, confirm, schedule, assign, notes, price, payment link), what is missing for a recurring-plan business (no recurring series or next-visit scheduling, no customer record across requests, no crew assignment on the calendar, no SMS, no reminders), the time clock for cleaners (Spanish, phone use, forgotten clock-outs), the credits tab, team management, search, exports, and the risk of the owner doing something irreversible. Report prioritised product gaps and UX defects with the lines that would change.

Audit the pricing model and its presentation as a pricing analyst: extract docs/MKG-pricing-logic.pdf with pdftotext (and read docs/make-pricing-pdf.py) and compare it line by line with plans.js (base, per-unit, discounts, follow-up tiers, visitsPerMonth, maxPercentOfVisit, referral amounts, policy) and with what app.js and quote.js compute and display on index.html, plans.html, quote.html and the commercial pages. Check: the formula and rounding; whether the numbers are plausible for Charlotte (e.g. Essentials 1 bed 1 bath one-time at $111, Complete 7 bed 6 bath weekly, commercial 20000 sqft every weekday), minimum charges, first-visit or deep-clean pricing being 'quoted individually' while the plan estimator implies a first visit at the plan rate, the monthly figure math, discount ladder monotonicity, the follow-up tier 'uses' indirection, tax, travel or parking fees, add-ons, and what the request payload stores (estimatePerVisit, estimateOneVisit, estimateFullPrice, estimatePerMonth, discount) versus what the admin sees and the client is promised ('price confirmed before the first visit'). Report inconsistencies, risky promises, and presentation issues, anchored to files and lines, and flag which items need the owner's decision.

Audit privacy.html, terms.html, the i18n.js terms.* and privacy.* keys, refer.html, and the claims on every page against what the code actually does and against common US/North Carolina small-business practice: data actually collected and where it goes (Firestore in nam5, Formspree, Google Fonts, Google reCAPTCHA Enterprise via App Check whose terms require a visible notice and links on pages where it runs, Firebase Auth, Stripe payment links, localStorage and sessionStorage usage), a cookie or storage notice, data retention and deletion requests, children, the referral program terms (who qualifies, repeat customers, stacking, expiry, cash value), the 24-hour cancellation policy and late-cancel charge consistency between terms.html, plans.js policy.changeNoticeHours, account.js and the FAQ, SMS and 'text us' consent (TCPA) and whether the contactMethod text option implies the business will text customers, email marketing, the 'established 2014' and insurance claims, the no-contracts promise versus commercial clients, accessibility statement, copyright year, business legal name and address (a service-area business with no address), the Spanish legal text being a faithful translation, and anything the site promises that the code cannot deliver. Report concrete gaps anchored to files and lines; this is not legal advice but a checklist for the owner and their lawyer.

Using docs/PLAN.md as the brief and the README as the status, assess what the live site still lacks to compete for Charlotte cleaning customers and to grow: compare the plan's site architecture (services page, about, contact, reviews, careers, content) with the 13 pages that exist; trust-building without invented reviews (team photos, before/after, a real Google Business Profile link and review collection flow, insurance statement, guarantee wording), a services or add-ons page, a first-clean offer, gift cards, local SEO landing pages by neighbourhood or suburb (Matthews, Huntersville, Ballantyne, Fort Mill), bilingual marketing, a client confirmation email and SMS reminders (the only email today goes to the owner), online payment beyond a bare Stripe link, recurring-visit scheduling and plan management, a hiring page for cleaners, analytics (there is none: no GA4, no conversion events, no error reporting), social links, a blog or tips page, and whether the referral program is discoverable before sign-in. For each gap say what it would gain, what it costs, and which file or page it touches. Rank by expected effect on bookings.

scope: hosting and CI, maintainability, rendered smoke tests, email notifications, documentation, and resilience

finders.prompt: Audit firebase.json, .firebaserc, .github/workflows/firebase-hosting-merge.yml and firebase-hosting-pull-request.yml, robots.txt, sitemap.xml and the repo layout as the deployment pipeline: what the ignore list actually deploys (list the files Hosting would publish; check docs, brand/source, brand/*.py, README, vendor, .github, firestore.rules, the pricing PDF, make-pages.py); the headers block (max-age=0 on all html/js/css despite ?v= busting; no headers for images or fonts; no security headers: Content-Security-Policy or at least frame-ancestors, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy needed for Google sign-in popups); missing cleanUrls and trailingSlash; missing redirects (www to apex, /index.html to /); no 404.html; firebase.json declaring firestore.rules while the deploy action only publishes hosting (rules drift, manual paste per SETUP doc); the merge workflow's secret check and checkout ordering, floating action versions (@v0), no lint, no HTML validation, no link check, no preview smoke test; the PR workflow exposing the service account to same-repo PRs; no dependabot or branch protection notes; the .firebaserc project id. Report with lines and concrete config suggestions.

Audit maintainability: run docs/make-pages.py into a scratch directory (never into the repo; read it first to see how to point it elsewhere, or copy the repo to your scratch dir and run it there) and diff its output against the committed availability.html, account.html, admin.html, privacy.html and terms.html to detect drift; compare the header and footer markup across all 13 pages for inconsistencies (nav items, links, aria labels, the ?v= version numbers on every script and stylesheet tag across files: are they all 22?); check README.md statements against the code (e.g. the logo note, the 'Before launch' list, which pages exist, what the owner edits); run eslint (flat config in your scratch dir with browser globals, no-undef, no-unused-vars, eqeqeq, no-redeclare) over the site JS and triage real issues; look for dead code, unused i18n keys and CSS rules, duplicated helpers (esc, dollars, $ selectors) across files, magic strings for statuses and slot ids, the single 1776-line i18n.js, and the absence of package.json, tests, or a CHANGELOG. Report issues that will cause mistakes when the owner or a future developer edits the site, with lines.

Run a rendered smoke test of the whole site with Playwright against http://127.0.0.1:8787/: for all 13 pages, in EN and ES, at 390px and 1280px: capture console errors and warnings, uncaught exceptions, failed or 404 network requests (including every image, script, font, favicon and the Firebase reserved URLs that 404 locally: note which are expected), elements whose text still equals an i18n key or contains an unreplaced {placeholder}, empty elements that should have content (data-business, data-i18n), crawl every internal href and anchor (#id exists on the target page?) and every link in sitemap.xml and robots.txt, test the language toggle round trip and that ?lang=es persists across navigation, drive the estimator and the plan selection, walk the residential and commercial quote flows to the demo confirmation with valid input and try invalid input at each step (what message appears, is it translated), open availability.html and pick a day and slot and confirm it carries into the quote, open refer.html, and load account.html and admin.html to see the not-connected messaging. Save scripts and screenshots to your scratch dir. Report every defect with page, viewport, language, and the file/line responsible; list expected-local-only failures separately so they are not counted.

Audit the owner-notification and messaging flow: app.js notify() and the Formspree POST (headers, JSON shape, the _subject field, _replyto or email field for Reply-To, what Formspree will show in the email body for lists and nested values, the language of the email, date and time formatting and time zone in the email, the link back to admin.html), quote.js mailFields(), the Promise.race 8-second timeout and what happens on Formspree failure or quota (silent? the visitor sees success?), account.js move and cancel emails, the absence of any email or SMS to the client (confirmation, reminder, receipt, note-from-owner notification), the Firebase Auth email templates (sender noreply@<project>.firebaseapp.com, deliverability and spam, English only, action URL landing on account.html), the public endpoint abuse surface, and the tab-title counter on admin.html as the only 'notification'. Also evaluate the owner's realistic response flow on a phone: can they reply, call, text from the email or admin card with one tap? Report concrete gaps and defects anchored to lines, with suggestions (Trigger Email extension, Formspree features, Twilio, etc.) and their costs.

Audit the documentation as the only onboarding a future maintainer or the owner has: README.md, docs/SETUP-firebase.md, docs/PLAN.md, the long comments at the top of plans.js, backend.js, firestore.rules, styles.css and docs/make-pages.py. Check every factual statement against the code and configuration (which pages exist, what the owner edits, which steps are done, the 'Before launch' list items that are already done or stale, the logo note, the serviceArea note, whether firebase.json truly does not deploy rules, how ?v= versions are bumped, how to run locally and with the emulator, the emulator=1 query flag, how to regenerate pages), missing runbooks (changing prices safely, rotating the Formspree endpoint or the App Check key, exporting or backing up Firestore, handling a data-deletion request, adding a slot or weekday, closing for a holiday, what to do when Firebase bills, rolling back a bad deploy, enforcing App Check), secrets hygiene (service account JSON, the appCheckKey and Formspree id being public by design: is that stated?), licence attribution for vendor/qrcode.js (MIT requires the licence text), the pricing PDF being out of sync, and contradictions between documents. Report each inaccuracy or gap with the file and line.

Audit resilience and degraded modes in backend.js, app.js, quote.js, account.js, admin.js, availability.js, calendar.js, i18n.js: Firebase SDK script load failure or partial load (script() chain, async=false ordering), init.json missing or slow, App Check activate throwing, Firestore permission-denied and unavailable errors (which user-facing message, is it translated, is there a retry), the 'not connected' fallback silently showing every window as open on the live site if init fails (a visitor books a full slot), the quote submit paths when Firestore succeeds and Formspree fails or vice versa, offline and flaky mobile networks (Firestore persistence not enabled, listeners never resolving, spinners), localStorage or sessionStorage unavailable (private mode) in every try/catch and the places with no try/catch, JavaScript disabled (no noscript; the dial and prices never appear), very old browsers (ES2015+ syntax or APIs used without fallback: Promise, fetch, Object.assign, Array.prototype.includes, optional chaining, template literals, String.padStart, Intl), ad blockers blocking Firebase, reCAPTCHA or Formspree domains, Google Fonts blocked, slow 3G timings, version skew between cached JS and new rules, and double-click or rapid re-submits. Reproduce what you can in Chromium with route blocking and offline mode; report with lines.
